source: NCERT Class IX, India and the Contemporary World I, History Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. France before 1789
points: France was an **absolute monarchy** under **Louis XVI** (of the **Bourbon** dynasty); a deep **financial crisis** (wars, extravagance, aid to the American Revolution).

sub: **First Estate — clergy**; **Second Estate — nobility** (both exempt from most taxes).
**Third Estate — everyone else** (peasants, workers, middle class/bourgeoisie) — bore the burden of **taxes** (e.g. **taille**).

points: **Enlightenment philosophers** inspired new ideas: **Rousseau** (Social Contract), **Montesquieu** (Spirit of the Laws — separation of powers), **Voltaire**.

sections.heading: 2. The Outbreak (1789)
points: Louis XVI called the **Estates General** (May 1789) to raise taxes; the **Third Estate** demanded **voting by head** (not by estate).
They formed the **National Assembly** and took the **Tennis Court Oath** to draft a constitution.
On **14 July 1789**, an angry crowd **stormed the Bastille** prison — the symbolic start of the Revolution (now France's **National Day**).

sections.heading: 3. Key Developments
points: **Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen (1789)** — liberty, equality, right to property, freedom of speech.
France became a **constitutional monarchy** (Constitution of **1791**), with separation of powers.
**1792:** monarchy abolished, France declared a **Republic**; Louis XVI **executed (1793)**.
**The Jacobins** under **Robespierre** led the **Reign of Terror (1793–94)** — mass executions by the **guillotine**; ended with Robespierre's own execution.

sections.heading: 4. Legacy
points: The motto **'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity'** spread across Europe and the world.
**Napoleon Bonaparte** rose to power (crowned Emperor 1804), spread revolutionary laws (Napoleonic Code) before his fall (1815).
**Slavery** was abolished in French colonies (finally under the Revolution's ideals in 1848).
Inspired **democracy, nationalism and human rights** worldwide.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 1789; Louis XVI (Bourbon); Three Estates (clergy, nobility, Third Estate — taxed).
Philosophers: Rousseau, Montesquieu (separation of powers), Voltaire.
Storming of the Bastille = 14 July 1789 (National Day).
Declaration of Rights of Man 1789; Republic 1792; Louis XVI executed 1793.
Robespierre = Reign of Terror (guillotine); motto = Liberty, Equality, Fraternity; Napoleon crowned 1804.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Third Estate** bore taxes; the **first two estates** (clergy, nobility) were largely **exempt**.
**Montesquieu** gave the idea of **separation of powers** (Spirit of the Laws).
**Bastille stormed = 14 July 1789**; France became a **Republic in 1792**.
The **Reign of Terror** is linked to **Robespierre** and the **Jacobins**.
